precepts.text: In as much as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. When we biting and devouring each other, when you be angry with your brother without a cause, you slandering him: you're not slandering us, you slandering Christ, because Christ put us in this position.
precepts.point: When the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them. So they knew: damn, this negro talking about us. Rightfully so. And they still wanted to lay hands on him, because the words was cut and deep, and they knew that Christ would take away their place.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
In the parable the husbandmen, the Pharisees, beat the servants and killed the son. They knew who he was: “This is the heir; come, let us kill him.” To say that, they had to acknowledge the works of Christ and know this man is the Messiah, and they still rejected him.

Christ shows where that same hatred lands today: “Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.” If you do anything to one of these men, even give them a sip of water, you do it unto Christ.

Some of these black Hebrew Israelites right now may say, well, brother, we not talking about Yahawashi, we not talking about Christ; our anger is towards you, we slander you. No. When we are biting and devouring each other, when you are angry with your brother without a cause, when you slander and hate, you are not slandering us. You are slandering Christ, because Christ put us in this position.

The only difference is we can't do nothing about it. We are going to stay in the spirit and continue to do what God called us to do. Christ can do something about it. He can do a lot of things. That's why they call him the king of terrors, and the stone that falls on the wicked husbandmen “will grind him to powder.”

precepts.text: The parable of the talents: the man who hid his talent in the earth did nothing with the understanding God gave him, and his Lord called him a wicked and slothful servant, and said, take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security; realize that when you do not utilize that gift, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take this truth even further. If you cannot be used, you are useless; and none of you are useless, because we all have been called for a reason. There is something in you that you have to give to the nation.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.
precepts.why:
We have to utilize the gifts God gives us in this truth. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security. Realize that when you don't use it, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take the truth even further. The parable of the talents shows it; the talent is money, standing for the understanding God bestows on you.

“Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth”. He hid that understanding, that gift, and did nothing with it.

Watch what Christ says: “Thou wicked and slothful servant”. “Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.” Even if you couldn't do anything else, you could have put it with the exchangers so something could be reaped. “Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.”

We have seen it time and again: brothers and sisters with talents who hide them, or hold them over us: you can't do this without me. Know that yes, it can be done without you. If you can't be used, you are useless. But none of you are useless. We all have been called for a reason; there is something in you that you have to give to build the nation. The quicker we understand that, the quicker we get out of here.

precepts.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father.
precepts.point: Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

precepts.why:
The foolish virgins came afterward saying, “Lord, Lord, open to us”, and were answered, “Verily I say unto you, I know you not.” Christ had already said who gets in: “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”

Saying Lord, Lord is not enough. The foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them, and the oil is the wisdom of the scriptures. Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord, and the door is shut on them.

The one who enters is the one who does the will of the Father. That is the difference between the wise and the foolish.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. That is the will of the Father, and the foolish did not have it.
precepts.point: Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

precepts.why:
What is the will of the Father that the foolish did not do? David says it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of the Father is his law, kept in the heart.

That is the oil the wise took in their vessels with their lamps, the wisdom of the scriptures, and the foolish did not have it. When the cry came at midnight, the wise were ready and went in with the bridegroom, and the foolish were left outside saying Lord, Lord. Watch therefore: have the law within your heart, because no one knows the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.
